results.title: Metrology, Inspection, and Process Control XXXIX | (2025) | Publications | SPIE
results.content: As an inline metrology tool, CD-SEM (Critical Dimension Scanning Electron Microscope) needs to provide accurate segmentation of SEM images to ensure precise measurement of semiconductor layers. Experiments conducted on Intel 18A PowerVia wafers demonstrated that these methods significantly improve image resolution, CD measurement robustness, and process control suitability for both development and high-volume manufacturing environments. This work introduces a task-agnostic, meta-learning approach aimed at addressing this challenge, which enables the incremental addition of new defect classes and scales to create a more robust and generalized model for semiconductor defect inspection.We have benchmarked our approach using real resist-wafer SEM (Scanning Electron Microscopy) datasets for two process steps, ADI and AEI, and two distinct geometric patterns as Line-Space (LS) and Hexagonal Contact-Hole Directed-Self-Assembly (HEXCH-DSA), demonstrating its superior performance compared to conventional supervised training methods. To demonstrate this approach, we chose a challenging, high-precision dataset from advanced nanometer-scale semiconductor manufacturing, where ultra-high-resolution (UHR) Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) images are critical for precise pattern fidelity assessment and Optical Proximity Correction (OPC) modeling.
